directAnswer: A website may not be working due to server issues, DNS problems, or browser-related errors.
summary: This page outlines common reasons a website might not function properly, along with troubleshooting steps and FAQs.

sections.heading: Server Issues
sections.body: If the server hosting the website is down or experiencing high traffic, the site may not load. Check the server status or contact the hosting provider.

sections.heading: DNS Problems
sections.body: Domain Name System (DNS) issues can prevent a website from resolving. Verify your DNS settings and try flushing your DNS cache.

sections.heading: Browser Errors
sections.body: Sometimes, browser extensions or cached data can interfere with website loading. Try accessing the site in incognito mode or clearing your browser cache.

steps.title: Check Server Status
steps.detail: Use a website like 'Down For Everyone Or Just Me?' to see if the site is down globally.

steps.title: Flush DNS Cache
steps.detail: On Windows, open Command Prompt and type 'ipconfig /flushdns'. On macOS, use 'sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder' in Terminal.

steps.title: Clear Browser Cache
steps.detail: In most browsers, access settings and look for 'Clear Browsing Data' to remove cached files.

steps.title: Disable Extensions
steps.detail: Temporarily disable browser extensions to see if they are causing the issue.

faqs.question: How can I tell if the problem is on my end?
faqs.answer: Try accessing the website from a different device or network to determine if the issue is local.

faqs.question: What should I do if the website is still down?
faqs.answer: Contact the website's support team or check their social media for updates on outages.

faqs.question: Could my antivirus software be blocking the website?
faqs.answer: Yes, some antivirus programs may block access to certain websites. Check your antivirus settings.

caveats: Different browsers and operating systems may have varying methods for clearing cache or disabling extensions.
